simple.meaning: אַגְמוֹן (ʼagmôwn) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a rush (as growing there); collectively a rope of rushes.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Job 40:26. The surrounding context includes Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אַגְמוֹן (H100) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אַגְמוֹן (ʼagmôwn) / H100 is traced through Job 40:26, Job 41:12, Isaiah 9:13, Isaiah 19:15 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.short: a rush (as growing there); collectively a rope of rushes
definitions.full: H100. agmon אַגְמוֺן אַגְמֹן, noun [masculine] rush, bulrush . 1 used as cord or line Job 40:26 (of twisted rushes, or spun of rush-fibre, compare Di on the passage); as fuel Job 41:12 ; simile of bending head Isa 58:5 . 2 metaphor of the lowly, insignif . (|| כִּמָּה ) Isa 9:13 ; 19:15 . אגן (probably circular, round , compare Arabic ball of cheek & see Talmud אוֺגֶן curved rim of a vessel ).
definitions.rootNote: from the same as 98 ; a marshy pool (others from a different root, a kettle ); by implication
